study.title: End-to-End Deep Learning Model for Cardiac Cycle Synchronization from Multi-View Angiographic Sequences
study.venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)

imaging.modality_detail: Raw coronary X-ray angiography videos (free breathing), 1024x1024, 15 or 30 fps
imaging.territory_detail: Left or right coronary artery, pediatric patients
imaging.frames_per_sequence: 117.8 frames on average (53.6 after contrast-based frame selection); 15 or 30 fps

task.task_description: Cardiac cycle synchronization of two angiographic sequences from different views: a finetuned CNN extracts per-frame cardiac-phase features from 3-frame stacks, a cosine similarity matrix between videos is built, and Dijkstra pathfinding finds temporally coherent frame correspondences; evaluated against ECG R-wave derived ground truth.
task.clinical_application: ECG-free temporal matching of multi-view coronary angiograms as a prerequisite for dynamic 3D+T coronary reconstruction

temporal_evidence.quote: stacked in groups of 3 consecutive images to create small sequences that are used as inputs to the model

method.pretraining: ImageNet-pretrained CNN finetuned on angiographic data

metrics.metric: Normalized synchronization path score (accuracy vs ECG), mean
Normalized path score, simultaneous biplane pairs
metrics.task: cardiac cycle synchronization, biplane subgroup (8 pairs)

metrics.metric: Normalized path score after trimming first and last points

G3.quote: this method removes the temporal dimension of the angiographic sequences, which prevent the extraction of functional information

G4.quote: Since a single view of CA cannot show every detail of the whole coronary tree, multiple sequences are recorded from different angles

G5.quote: A novel loss function, called the soft pair loss, is proposed for training a neural network from weakly-annotated data

other_limitations: About 5% of synchronization paths score under 0.85
Pathfinding deviates from ground truth at sequence boundaries
Lower path scores between R-wave peaks (end of systole)
ECG-derived ground truth imprecise at end of systole; uncorrected R-peak detection errors
future_work: Trim first and last frames of synchronized pairs
Use synchronization as basis for 3D reconstruction of the coronary tree
